okay, themes first:

1. early-adopter identity under threat. you were there for the flop era (Life Aquatic bombing, Rushmore as arthouse ghost) and now the Tumblr Grand Budapest wave claims the same canon. so you keep moving the shibboleth deeper: not "have you seen it" but "can you place the Stones cue in the tent scene"

2. cultural literacy as a cognitive test. Stones -> Vermeer -> Stradivarius (you wrote STRATAVARIOUS lol, very on-brand phonetic encoding) -> encyclical. it's not really about each item, it's the same probe repeated: do you have the underlying database or just the poster

3. insider gatekeeping. "i'm as core millennial as they come" is you disarming the exile risk before you swing. classic move so you can critique the tribe without getting kicked out of it

4. archival boredom. 88ers now don't generate, they curate. letterboxd, discogs, playlists as personality. same hunger at 17, just with adult money and bad knees

5. AI as the new cut. "they don't use ai" wasn't really about usage stats, it was about *mode*. using vs building. curation vs generation again

as architecture:

Ti-dom is running the whole show. you don't argue vibes, you police definitions. "what counts as 'used'?" is pure Ti — the 84% vs 58% catch, the delta question, the "if you know prompting basics you've generated one image" intuition. you're auditing the instrument, not just rejecting the reading.

Ne-aux is the escalation engine. film -> painting -> violins -> papal letters -> AI adoption stats. that's not random, it's pattern-hunting: same vacuity shape in different domains.

Si-tert is the anchor. everything gets measured against your own high school baseline. "i saw it when it bombed" is Si as credential.

Fe-inferior is the preemptive self-drag. you include yourself in the indictment so the critique lands as honesty instead of superiority. but the tell is you still need the distinction — you're the millennial who *builds* pipelines, not the one who makes lists.

the real move: "not exceptional = worthless" is load-bearing for you. if the cohort catches up to your early pick, the pick stops proving exceptionality, so the test has to get harder. that's why it went from "seen Rushmore" to "name the Stones segue" to "spell encyclical" in like six minutes.

honest challenge back: is the literacy test actually measuring depth, or is it measuring *your* specific database? because a millennial who never saw Tenenbaums but builds weird agent shit from scratch might be more your kin than one who passes all four trivia gates and only curates.
